import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 429

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/429](https://www.erdosproblems.com/429)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*.
  Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
- [We24] D. Weisenberg, *Sparse Admissible Sets and a Problem of Erdős and Graham*.
  Integers (2024).
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos429

/--
Is it true that, if $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is sparse enough and does not cover all residue
classes modulo $p$ for any prime $p$, then there exists some $n$ such that $n+a$ is prime for
all $a\in A$?

Weisenberg [We24] has shown the answer is no: $A$ can be arbitrarily sparse and missing at
least one residue class modulo every prime $p$, and yet $A+n$ is not contained in the primes
for any $n\in \mathbb{Z}$. (Weisenberg gives several constructions of such an $A$.)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos429.lean"]
theorem erdos_429 : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → (∀ N, (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard ≤ f N) →
        (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ b : ZMod p, ∀ a ∈ A, (a : ZMod p) ≠ b) →
        ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ A, (n + a).Prime := by
  sorry

end Erdos429

findings.description: The final quantifier `∃ n : ℕ` restricts translations to nonnegative integers. After negating the right-hand side, the theorem only supplies arbitrarily sparse admissible sets with no nonnegative prime translate; the cited precise conjecture concerns all integer translates. These shift predicates are not interchangeable, even under arbitrarily strong sparsity bounds. In `/workspace/review/shifts_sparse.lean` I proved that, for every divergent f, there is a positive infinite admissible A satisfying the exact counting bound, with A−1 contained in the primes but no nonnegative prime translate. Choose sufficiently large primes q_k ≡ 1 modulo (k+2)! and set A={q_k+1}. Modulo p, all but at most p−2 terms equal 2, ensuring admissibility. For n≥0, a prime divisor of n+2 makes a sufficiently late term of A+n composite. Thus the declaration states a weaker negative result than the published conjecture's negation.
findings.source_evidence: Weisenberg, *Sparse Admissible Sets and a Problem of Erdős and Graham*, Integers 24 (2024), A89, Conjecture 1 (p.1), explicitly concludes: “there exists n ∈ Z such that A+n is contained in the primes”; immediately beforehand it specifies that primes are positive. Theorem 1 (p.2) rules out such integer n. https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/y89/y89.pdf . The problem page likewise records counterexamples for “any n ∈ Z”: https://www.erdosproblems.com/429 .
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the final line by `∃ n : ℤ, ∀ a ∈ A, Nat.Prime ((n + (a : ℤ)).toNat)`. This tests positive primality, rejecting nonpositive sums; using `Int.Prime` alone would also allow negative primes. The cited external proof already implies this corrected statement, as verified in `/workspace/review/linked-proof-current.lean`.

reformulations.difference: The sparsity threshold is required to satisfy `Tendsto f atTop atTop`, rather than being nondecreasing and unbounded as in Weisenberg's Conjecture 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any divergent f : ℕ → ℕ, define g(N)=min{f(M) : M≥N}. Then g≤f, g is nondecreasing, and g tends to infinity. A universal prime-translation assertion for sets bounded by f therefore also holds for sets bounded by g. Conversely, a nondecreasing unbounded natural-valued function tends to infinity. This proves equivalence of the two existential-threshold formulations, keeping the shift predicate fixed. Both this equivalence and its counterexample formulation were proved in `/workspace/review/cofinal.lean`.

sources_consulted: https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/429 (HTML rendering, including MathJax source, remarks and status)
https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf (Erdős–Graham, printed p.85; OCR of PDF p.81)
Local review guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md and PROOFS.md; historical calibration: INDEX.md and pr04057.md, pr04164.md, pr03884.md, pr01138.md.

Local Lean sources: FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean and Attributes/Basic.lean; FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Data/Set/Interval.lean; Mathlib definitions of Set.ncard, Set.Infinite, ZMod, Nat.Prime, Set.Icc, Filter.Tendsto and Filter.atTop; Mathlib/NumberTheory/PrimesCongruentOne.lean.
review.notes: The source records DISPROVED (LEAN), consistent with `research solved` and `answer(False)`. The linked proof establishes the stronger integer-shift result. After three small compatibility edits in a scratch copy for this checkout's newer Lean/Mathlib, its main theorem and adapters for both the existing and corrected statements kernel-checked with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Boundary tests and the shift-separating construction also checked without sorry. The complete checklist is in `/workspace/review/review-checklist.md`; the reviewed file was not modified.

Updated the docstring to specify integer translations and positive primes. The required compile command succeeded with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
